content.text:
I migrated all four service modules to the repository pattern, one at a time, running each module's tests before starting the next. Each module's tests pass (2/2), and the full suite passes (10/10). No file in `src/services/` imports `db.js` any more.

| Module | Repository used | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `auth-service.js` | `UserRepository` (new method `findActiveByEmail`) | 2/2 |
| `order-service.js` | `OrderRepository` | 2/2 |
| `payment-service.js` | **new** `PaymentRepository` (`findByOrder`, `findUncaptured`) | 2/2 |
| `user-service.js` | `UserRepository` | 2/2 |

The exported functions now return promises instead of taking callbacks, and the four service test files use `async`/`await`.

Changes beyond the services and their tests:
- **New repository:** `payments` had no repository, so I created `src/repositories/payment-repository.js`, modelled on the other two.
- **New method on `UserRepository`:** `auth-service` looks users up by email, and the repository had no method for that, so I added `findActiveByEmail`.
- **Router update:** `src/api/routes.js` passes callbacks to the services, so switching them to promises would have broken every route. I added a small `respond(promise, cb)` adapter there so the router still works the old way. The unit tests can't catch this kind of break because they call the services directly.

**Not verified:** I couldn't run `scripts/check-routes.js`, which calls each route the way the router does. The command needed approval and wasn't granted, so the router change has been read but not executed. Run `node scripts/check-routes.js` to check it.

Nothing is committed; the changes are in the working tree on `main`.
